leapTableRevision: ierc-2026-09-06 (IANA leap-seconds.list updated through IERS Bulletin C; file expires 2027-06-28)
description: TAI-UTC offset steps (positive leap seconds) as a function of the POSIX UTC label at which each step becomes effective. This file is the single versioned source of truth for UTC<->TT conversion. Refresh process (build-time, never runtime): fetch https://data.iana.org/time-zones/data/leap-seconds.list (IERS Bulletin C derived; authoritative origin https://www.iers.org/IERS/EN/Publications/Bulletins/bulletinc.html), diff the DTAI rows against the entries below, bump leapTableRevision, commit, and record the retrieval date in tools/spikes/s0.7/report.json. ECMAScript Date cannot represent a UTC label with a leap second (23:59:60); POSIX labels therefore skip the inserted second, and the offset column changes exactly at the effective date label.

provenance.sourceNote: IANA tzdata leap-seconds.list, '#$ last update' NTP timestamp 3992312697, '#@ file expires' NTP timestamp 4023129600 = 2027-06-28; file states it is updated through IERS Bulletin C (IERS origin: https://hpiers.obspm.fr/iers/bul/bulc/bulletinc.dat).
provenance.verifiedPoints: Entry count 28 (base 10 s at 1972-01-01 + 27 steps); 2017-01-01 -> 37 s; no entry dated after 2017-01-01 as of retrieval, so offset 37 s is in force throughout 2026. Re-verified 2026-09-06 against the live IANA file: all 28 DTAI rows matched date-by-date and value-by-value, last update 3992312697, expiry 4023129600 (2027-06-28), no negative step.
provenance.negativeLeapContingency: No negative leap second has ever been inserted (all rows type=positive). A negative-leap policy is an open item (ADR-008): the adapter would need a 'negative' row whose POSIX label SET repeats 23:59:59 once, which the POSIX timeline cannot express - the schema reserves the type field for it.
